title: The English settlement of Barbados
summary: The first English ship touched Barbados on 14 May 1625 under John Powell and the island was claimed for James I; the lasting settlement began on 17 February 1627 near what is now Holetown, when the William and John landed a party under Henry Powell of eighty settlers and ten English indentured labourers, with about forty enslaved Taíno brought from Guyana to plant. It was a proprietary colony funded by the London merchant Sir William Courten, so the first colonists were his tenants. Tobacco was the export. Nothing in this yet is a sugar island.
